title: Designing Microfluidic Devices for Studying Cellular Responses Under Single or Coexisting Chemical/Electrical/Shear Stress Stimuli
protocol: Draw patterns to be ablated on PMMA substrates and double-side tapes using commercial software.
To study chemical concentrations and shear stresses, draw a "Christmas tree" pattern with varying width at its end in each of the five culture areas.
To study chemical concentrations and electric fields, draw a "Christmas tree" pattern including two more fluidic channels for salt bridges.
Turn on the CO2 laser scriber and check its connection to the computer.
Open the pattern to be ablated using commercial software.
Place a PMMA sheet or double-side tape on top of the stage in the laser scriber.
Adjust the focus of the CO2 laser if necessary, using the calibration bar and visible He-Ne laser.
Load the pattern into the scriber for ablation on the PMMA sheet or tape.
Pick up the patterned sheet or tape after ablation.
Remove unwanted pieces from the patterned sheet or tape.
Clean the surface with nitrogen blowing.
Attach acrylic adaptors to the top-most layer of the chip using super glue.
Assemble the microfluidic chip inside a laminar flow hood.
Attach 3 sheets of scribed PMMA sheets using 2 pieces of scribed double-sided tape.
Add one more piece of 0.07 mm thick double-sided tape to the bottom of the chip and attach it to a 10 cm diameter Petri dish.
Place the assembly chip in the vacuum chamber for overnight.
Attach the PMMA sheet to a double-sided tape of thickness = 0.22 mm for the CEF chip.
Expose the assembled chip inside the hood to UV for 30 min for sterilization.
Autoclave all tubes and nuts at 121 °C for 15 min prior to usage.
Connect the inlets to two 3-ml syringes via plastic tubes and finger-tight nuts.
Connect the outlet to a waste tube via a plastic tube and a finger-tight nut.
Depress the plunger on the syringe slowly to prime the fluidic channels with PBS.
Push syringes back and forth to remove bubbles.
Put the chips inside an incubator overnight at 37 °C under 5% CO₂.
Take the chip out of the incubator.
Dissolve 3% low melting point agarose in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) buffer using a microwave.
Inject solution-phased agarose into the salt bridge channel and insert the electrodes before solution solidifies.
Place silver/silver-chloride electrodes into the tubular nuts.
Connect the syringes to the syringe pumps.
Continuously flow the culture medium (Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s medium, DMEM) into the fluidic channel for 10 min at a flow rate of 20 μl/min to replace PBS.
Pre-warm 1x PBS in a 37 °C water bath before usage.
Pre-warm culture medium (DMEM plus FBS) in a 37 °C water bath before usage.
Pre-warm trypsin in a 37 °C water bath before usage.
Plate 2 x 10⁵ lung cancer CL1-5 cells in a 10 cm Petri dish supplied with DMEM plus 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Incubate the cells inside an incubator under 5% CO₂ at 37 °C until 90% confluence.
Aspirate the medium from the Petri dish.
Wash the cells once with pre-warmed 1x PBS.
Add 2 ml of 0.05% trypsin buffer to the cells and wait for 2 to 3 min at 37 °C to detach the cells.
Transfer cells to a 15 ml sterile centrifugation tube.
Add 6 ml of culture medium into the tube.
Gently invert the tube for mixing.
Take out 5 µl of the cell-containing medium for counting the cell number in a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 x g for 5 min.
Suspend 10^6 cells in 1 ml of culture medium.
Place the cell-containing medium in a 1 ml syringe.
Infuse the cell-containing medium into the microfluidic chip from the outlet.
Ensure that the solution distributes throughout the five culture areas.
Incubate the chip inside an incubator under 5% CO2 at 37 °C for 2 hr.
Take the chip out of the incubator.
Place the chip on top of a transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) glass heater.
Connect the ITO glass to a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller.
Maintain the temperature at 37 ± 0.5 °C via feedback from a thermal coupler clamped tightly between the ITO heater and the chip.

Put the chip-heater assembly on top of a motorized XY stage of an inverted microscope for tracking cell migration or a fixed XY stage of an inverted fluorescent microscope for measuring ROS production.
Generate two syringes with 5 ml of chemical solutions at concentrations 0 and 1 in culture medium.
Pump the concentration 0 solution into the chip at a flow rate of 0.3 ml/min for 1 hour in the CSS chip.
Pump the concentration 1 solution into the chip at a flow rate of 20 µl/min for 20 minutes followed by a flow rate of 20 µl/hr for another 120 minutes in the CEF chip.
Program the XY stage of the microscope to take photos every 15 minutes for 2 hours via a digital single-lens reflex (DSLR) camera.
Prepare the stock of 2′-7′-DCFDA at 10 mM in molecular biology grade dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Dilute DCFDA in DMEM to 5 µM without serum.

Pump 2′-7′-DCFDA (5 µM in DMEM) into the chip at a flow rate of 20 µl/min for 20 minutes followed by a flow rate of 20 µl/hr for another 20 minutes after the shear stress stimulus or electrical field stimulus.
Pump DMEM into the chip at a flow rate of 20 µl/hr for 20 minutes to wash the chip.
Take photos via a charge-coupled device (CCD) camera of certain FOVs within culture areas.
Calculate chemical concentrations in the five culture areas for both CSS chip and CEF chip.
Assume smooth and equal splitting of liquids around forks to determine relative concentrations.
Generate concentrations of 0, 25, 100, 175, and 200 µM by injecting H2O2 at 0 and 200 µM from inlets.
Calculate shear stress (τ) within each culture area using the formula τ = Q * η / (h * w), where Q is volume flow rate, η is fluidic viscosity, h is channel height, and w is channel width.
Set parameters for CSS chip: Q = 0.3 ml/min per inlet (Q = 0.12 ml/min in each culture area), η = 0.0008 Pa·s, h = 1 mm, w ranging from 1 to 4 mm.
Calculate shear stress range from 0.0048 Pa for 4 mm wide region to 0.0192 Pa for 1 mm wide region.

In CEF chip, calculate EF strength within each culture area using E = I / (σ * Aeff), where I is electric current across the fluidic channel, σ is electrical conductivity of medium, and Aeff is effective cross-sectional area.
Run the ImageJ software.
Open a fluorescent image for analysis.
Change the image type to "16-bit" to convert it to grayscale.
Draw a polygon to enclose a cell in the image.
Measure the mean fluorescent intensity of the enclosed cell.
Repeat measurement steps to collect intensities from at least 50 cells of three independent experiments.
Calculate the mean intensity with standard error of mean (SEM).
Repeat steps 6.1.1 to 6.1.4 for each experimental condition.
Analyze cell migration using ImageJ software.
Open an image taken at time = 0 in ImageJ.
Draw a polygon to enclose a single cell.
Measure the center of mass of the cell as (x1, y1).
Repeat steps 6.2.1 and 6.2.2 to measure the center of mass of the same cell at time = t as (x2, y2).
Calculate the migration rate (in µm/hr) of this cell.
Collect migration rates from at least 50 cells in three independent experiments.
Calculate the mean migration rate with standard error of mean (SEM).
Measure the angle θ between the vector of the applied electric field and the vector from the start to end position of the cell.
Calculate the migration directedness of this cell as cosine θ.
Collect migration directedness data from at least 50 cells in three independent experiments.
Calculate the mean migration directedness with SEM for each experimental condition.
Run the ImageJ software.
Load an image for analysis using "File" → "Open".
Treat each cell as an ellipse and draw a line indicating the long axis of the cell.
Measure the angle β between the line and the horizontal EF direction using "Analyze" → "Measure".
Repeat steps to collect β from at least 50 cells in three independent experiments, calculating mean cosine β with SEM.
